item.title: Dubai Hotel Owner Al Habtoor Calls Out Trump Over ‘Dangerous’ Iran War
item.description: Khalaf Ahmad Al Habtoor’s comments carry weight because he is behind some of the UAE’s largest hotels and because he is one of the rare hoteliers to speak out about the war's disruption to business.

item.title: Heathrow’s Flight Emissions Have Dropped 7%, Third Runway Closer Than Ever
item.description: The race is on to push Heathrow’s expansion plans through regulation and planning. But the airport’s case for a third runway relies heavily on sustainable aviation fuel and aviation still faces major challenges scaling the technology needed to decarbonize.

item.title: When the Sky Closes: A Decision Framework for Middle East Destination Recovery
item.description: Iran’s retaliatory strikes hit Middle East destinations’ civilian infrastructure. The region’s $460 billion tourism machine is counting the cost. This paper provides both the diagnosis and the decision architecture for what comes next.

item.title: How Creator Monoculture Is Hijacking Destination Identity
item.description: The entire incentive structure of the creator economy pushes toward exoticization over understanding, sensation over context.

item.title: Rare Plans Tech Expansion, B2C Growth With Samhi Hotels
item.description: Samhi Hotels' acquisition comes with a Marriott-led lifeline for Rare India, which has had to adapt significantly over two decades as experiential has grown in the region.

item.title: Airbnb Faces World Cup Shortfall in NYC — New Jersey Is Dominating
item.description: Nice try Airbnb, but New York authorities do not appear ready to even temporarily lift the ban on short-term rentals during the World Cup.

item.title: Iran War Is Costing Small Airlines $200,000 Daily, Insurer Estimates
item.description: Airlines have been impacted by the disruption caused by the war, and could now mitigate these costs by increasing future ticket pricing.

item.title: T20 World Cup Prompts Near 20-Fold Price Surge At Ahmedabad Hotels
item.description: It was never in doubt that Indians love to watch cricket. How much they're willing to spend to watch it live, is the more surprising part.

item.title: Shutdown Triggers TSA Staffing Shortages and Hours-Long Airport Lines
item.description: TSA staffing shortages are creating significantly long wait times at security as agents miss their first paycheck during the partial government shutdown.

item.title: Oil Price Shock Could Mean 10%+ Fare Hike, $24 Billion in Costs for U.S. Airlines
item.description: Jet fuel is the single largest expense for most airlines and executives will face pressure to respond soon with higher fares.
